items.item: The six anatomy/detail boards develop the selected frame and temples with consistent dimensions, module identities, openings, seams, hinges and folding geometry.
The material application and anatomy/detail views implement the material specification's exterior, interior and skin-contact assignments, treatments and colour codes.
All five contexts use the same selected glasses, component positions, physical controls, contact geometry, materials and colours as the anatomy and detail sources.
W1 and W3 place the nose and ear contacts consistently with the detail boards; W4 preserves the folded product's scale and frame/temple handling.
Assigned READY, CAPTURE and PRIVACY depictions follow the specified camera, light, slider and button behaviour, with charging off before W4 makes contact.
Case views and W4 preserve one case design, cavity, locating key, parallel mating interface, supports, finger access and folded-glasses scale.
Case dimensions, module envelopes, pad positions, contact polarity, materials and colours agree with the specification and folded-underside sources.
The case supports frame/temple regions without direct lens pressure; removal uses those regions, docking requires a closed slider, and amber indication begins only after contact.

requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

Show a complete adult eyewear concept with two transparent lenses without displays, a bridge, two folding temples, paired nose and ear contact regions, integrated components and identifiable physical controls. Form and hinge design may vary. Missing eyewear parts, display lenses, visibly intersecting folded temples or rigid modules crossing moving hinges fail; actual comfort is not established by a rendering.

Record 42 g as the maximum design target. Delivered drawings cannot establish measured mass, and the supplied facts explicitly leave mass unmeasured; this diagnostic does not require a weighing result or fail an image for apparent weight.

Interpret the concept as deliberate image capture followed by a user-initiated spoken question with paired-phone assistance. This input defines the interaction context without requiring an additional phone interface deliverable or proof of functioning electronics.

Each exploration board must name an alternative and show its complete glasses both open and folded with its own matching case. The three alternatives must differ recognisably in product design decisions such as frame, temples or case construction; merely changing names or recolouring the same concept is insufficient. Alternatives may legitimately differ from the subsequently selected design.

The written selection must resolve the three named explorations to one chosen concept and record its frame, temple and case decisions. That choice must be identified on the presentation's first page and govern both specifications. The documents must distinguish pre-selection alternatives from the developed choice. Rationale wording and document layout may vary; inconsistent choices or specifications describing an unexplained different concept fail.

Read actual chosen dimensions, not only allowable maxima: front width 140–150 mm; each hinge-axis-to-tip centreline length 135–150 mm; largest temple height/thickness at most 18/12 mm; folded envelope at most 150×60×48 mm; closed case at most 170×85×65 mm; and a defined usable cavity allowing at least 2 mm on all six sides except marked support/contact interfaces. Record both right-temple pad-centre distances within 60 mm, with P+ nearer the hinge and their difference 6 mm. Choices within the ranges are allowed; absent selected values or internally incompatible records fail.

The orthographic anatomy, folded underside and four case boards must repeat the specification's chosen open/folded dimensions and pad-centre positions. Their dimensional evidence must state the required 140–150 mm front and 135–150 mm temple ranges, 18×12 mm section limit, 150×60×48 mm folded limit, 170×85×65 mm case limit and actual cavity dimensions with six clearances of at least 2 mm, except marked support/contact interfaces. Across all six anatomy/detail boards, visible apertures, seams and hinge positions must describe one geometry. Enlargements and perspective changes are allowed; conflicting numbers, unmarked clearance exceptions or migrating features fail.

The sheet must record exactly one each of C01 28×8×5, B01 30×7×4, B02 30×7×4, S01 16×5×3, S02 16×5×3, K01 8×8×6, M01 4×3×2, I01 3×2×1, CB01 45×25×6, CC01 20×15×4 and U01 12×5×7 mm in local X/Y/Z order, plus schematic connections. C01 may occupy either temple; B01/S01 belong in the left temple and B02/S02 in the right, with speakers near ears; K01 belongs at an outer front corner, M01 in the frame or forward temple, I01 on the front beside K01, CB01/CC01 in the case and U01 at its wall. Preserve original envelopes under rotation, identify local orientations, and state at least 1 mm separation and enclosure with functional-opening exceptions. Missing modules, quantities, connections, incorrect dimensions or placement outside permitted regions fail.

Match all eight glasses IDs, local X/Y/Z dimensions and orientations on the orthographic anatomy to the component specification, and match all three case IDs and envelopes on the charging board. The anatomy must provide front/top/right views and schematic wiring. Show at least 1 mm envelope separation and enclosure except at functional openings, a 4 mm forward camera aperture and an outward front indicator centre within 12 mm of it. Batteries remain enclosed; speaker, microphone and U01 openings must occupy their recorded functional locations without moving rigid modules across hinges. A B01 explosion must show an accessible cover, detachable connection and removal arrow beside the exact replacement label. Rotation of intact envelopes is allowed; rescaled modules, insufficient space or an unserviceable illustrated battery fail.

Both documents must identify all three states and preserve their distinctions: READY means exposed camera, front light off and no active capture; CAPTURE means deliberate button operation, exposed camera and steady white front light; PRIVACY means an opaque slider covering the whole aperture, a visible position mark, front light off and camera/microphone capture inhibited even when the button is pressed. Text, diagrams or a state table may communicate the behaviour. Missing states, software-only privacy or contradictory light/capture behaviour fail.

Verify assigned W codes and state labels. W1 is an adult standing in a quiet urban pause, wearing open READY glasses in a three-quarter upper-body view with a nose/ear inset. W3 is an adult standing in a stationary sheltered transit waiting area with a clear READY temple side view; W1/W3 contact placement must match the detail boards. Both READY views expose the camera with its indicator off. CAPTURE shows deliberate reachable button use, an unobstructed camera and pressure-free lenses, and a steady white front indicator. W2 is worn PRIVACY at a desk, with a hand near the button, opaque full-aperture coverage, visible position mark, light off and camera/microphone inhibition on pressing. W4 shows the same fully folded shutter-closed glasses held by frame/temple regions above the same open case at a cafe table, at consistent scale and before contact, with charging indication off. Context styling may vary; incorrect sequence, grip, state or contact placement fails.

The charging and folded-underside boards must repeat two flush circular right-temple underside pads of 2 mm diameter, 6 mm centre spacing, matching 1.2 mm case tips and both recorded hinge distances within 60 mm, with P+ nearer the hinge. A mating section must establish corresponding polarity and parallel faces. Across the four case boards, preserve one keyed interior with lens-clear frame/temple supports, exposed case-wall input mouth and finger access. Charging shows fully folded shutter-closed glasses mated and a steady amber separate case indicator, using the internal battery without an external charging lead. Stored/idle shows the closed case with its externally visible indicator off and an empty open-case inset. The enlarged empty interior retains the same key, tips and supports; the removal sequence lifts fully folded glasses by frame/temple regions without lens pressure. View scale may change, but topology, polarity, seating and handling must agree.

Map the material specification onto identifiable exterior, interior and skin-contact surfaces of the selected glasses and case. Repeat its material names, treatments and colour codes, including satin TR90 shells, anodised aluminium hinges and silicone nose/ear contacts. Show rounded compliant contact zones separated from sharp edges, ports and charging pads. Case material and palette choices are open but must remain consistent with their recorded assignments. LUMA must appear on the anatomy glasses and stored case as actual product marking. Missing zoning, code disagreement or a required material replaced by another fails.

The material specification must provide materials, surface treatments, selected colour codes and contact-zone assignments sufficient to map exterior, interior and skin-contact surfaces. It must identify satin TR90 frame/temple shells, anodised aluminium hinges and silicone nose/ear contacts, plus the chosen case materials and finishes. The presentation must repeat those required assignments and selected codes consistently. Document layout may vary; a generic palette with no material zoning or conflicting assignments fails.

Each assigned board must provide its specified viewpoint or detail. Front three-quarter evidence must resolve the camera, slider, indicator and frame seams; rear three-quarter evidence must expose inner surfaces, hinges and contact zones. The underside must reveal the folded arrangement and right-temple pads. The nose detail must resolve the bridge and both rounded silicone contact regions. The ear/hinge detail must resolve compliant contact surfaces, outward/downward speaker openings near open ear canals and folding that keeps rigid modules wholly on one side of moving hinges. Cropping and enlargement are allowed when the assigned evidence remains readable; substituting redundant beauty views for the requested detail fails.

Review the complete 12-second video for the ordered progression READY, CAPTURE, PRIVACY, fully folded docking and closed-case stored/idle. READY exposes the camera with its light off; deliberate CAPTURE uses a reachable control without obstructing the camera or pressing lenses and shows steady white front light; PRIVACY fully covers the camera with an opaque marked slider, turns the light off and communicates camera/microphone inhibition. Dock only with the slider closed, using the same keyed seat, parallel matching contacts and lens-clear frame/temple supports. The separate case indicator becomes steady amber after mating and is visibly off on the closed stored case. Product dimensions, components, material assignments and colours must agree with the supplied source boards and specification. Editing and camera motion may vary; omitted or reordered states, changing product geometry, premature charging or contradictory privacy behaviour fail.
requirementChecks.manualReason: Inspect complete SHA-bound original outputs. This source draft contains no completed professional or model-output review; partial-frame/page sampling cannot prove whole-output compliance.

requirementChecks.criteria: The presentation must contain at least twelve pages and visibly incorporate identifiable content from every listed source, including all three directions, the selection, both specifications, six anatomy/detail boards, five operation/wearing boards, four case boards and material application. Include the LUMA-marked glasses and case views. Multiple sources may share a page, and legible cropping or re-layout is allowed; merely listing sources does not count. Missing source coverage, absent specifications, illegible identity-critical reuse or fewer than twelve pages fails.

The six anatomy/detail boards develop the selected frame and temples with consistent dimensions, module identities, openings, seams, hinges and folding geometry. The material application and anatomy/detail views implement the material specification's exterior, interior and skin-contact assignments, treatments and colour codes.

All five contexts use the same selected glasses, component positions, physical controls, contact geometry, materials and colours as the anatomy and detail sources. W1 and W3 place the nose and ear contacts consistently with the detail boards; W4 preserves the folded product's scale and frame/temple handling. Assigned READY, CAPTURE and PRIVACY depictions follow the specified camera, light, slider and button behaviour, with charging off before W4 makes contact.

Case views and W4 preserve one case design, cavity, locating key, parallel mating interface, supports, finger access and folded-glasses scale. Case dimensions, module envelopes, pad positions, contact polarity, materials and colours agree with the specification and folded-underside sources. The case supports frame/temple regions without direct lens pressure; removal uses those regions, docking requires a closed slider, and amber indication begins only after contact.
